# Story types

Stories is the theory-of-mind task: the child hears illustrated stories
and answers questions about what the characters know, believe, feel and
intend. Each story belongs to one scenario type, and the items are scored
with a two-parameter model, so items differ in how well they separate
children as well as in difficulty.

```{r tom-items}
tom_items <- items |>
  mutate(scenario = str_remove(coalesce(na_if(item_group_label, ""), item_group), " scenario$"))
tom_types <- tom_items |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(n_items = n(), difficulty = mean(difficulty),
            discrimination = median(discrimination), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(difficulty)
tom_low <- tom_items |> filter(discrimination < 0.5)
```

```{r tom-items-plot, fig.height=4.5}
#| label: fig-tom-items
#| fig-cap: "Calibrated difficulty and discrimination of each item, by scenario type."
tom_items |>
  ggplot(aes(x = difficulty, y = discrimination, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, lty = 3, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#4477AA", "#EE6677", "#228833", "#CCBB44", "#66CCEE", "#AA3377"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Item difficulty", y = "Discrimination") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

By mean difficulty, the easiest scenario type is
`r tom_types$scenario[1]` (`r f2(tom_types$difficulty[1])`) and the hardest
`r tom_types$scenario[nrow(tom_types)]` (`r f2(tom_types$difficulty[nrow(tom_types)])`).
`r nrow(tom_low)` of the `r nrow(tom_items)` items have a discrimination
below 0.5 and contribute little to a child's score
(`r paste(count(tom_low, scenario)$scenario, " ", count(tom_low, scenario)$n, collapse = ", ")`).
